chapter: Leaving the band, Strayhorn and reflections
title: Classical musicians who came to hear the band; the Capitol Theatre pit band
summary: Classical musicians admired the band; Greer and Duke studied the Capitol Theatre orchestra.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: Did many classical musicians come around and like the band?

All of them. All of them. You see, those long-haired musicians, you know, they loved what they heard. But they never played with us, so they used to come just to enjoy the music, being classical musicians. They'd come and enjoy the band, you know, all them guys. They were friends of Duke, they loved it, you know. Mutual admiration. I loved to hear them guys play.

I know when we first was in New York, small band, the Washingtonians they had the Capital Theater, big theater called the Capital Theater, 50th Street and Broadway. That was before, the music on the screen was synchronized, you know. They had the sound -- they had a big band, about 30, 35 pieces played in the Capital Theater pit. They used to play the music for the different pictures coming up. But man, they used -- especially newsreels, that's when them guys let out. Man, I remember we used to go -- it wasn't expensive then, we could go for 50 cents or something, sit up in the gallery. Me and Duke, we'd go and sit up there in the gallery and listen to them guys. And I was always watching them drummers because they had three of them, timpani, bass player and a snare drum player. But

them guys could make some changes fast, especially on the news reels. They were something to hear. And the trumpet player, ah, man, they had one fat guy, forget his name, he could hit all them high ones. Take out his hanky and pat his forehead, man, and sit back down. He was something.
But them drummers was talking. And man, I say, I liked that. I liked that. And shortly after when we went to the Cotton Club, all of them, there they are sitting out there.

Yeah, mutual admiration, you know. I think Duke got a lot -- you know, he was deep, a lot of ideas from listening to those cats. He never would ask you to show him something, no, his pride wouldn't allow that.
